cohort: Delivery records from women giving birth at a tertiary care hospital in Uttar Pradesh, India, between January 2011 and December 2021.
finding: The rate of Cesarean section at the tertiary care center significantly increased from 39.6% in 2011 to 52.4% in 2021, with oligohydramnios with intrauterine growth restriction being the most common indication for primary elective CS.
mod_finding: The overall Cesarean section rate experienced a significant rising trend over the decade, increasing from 39.6% to 52.4%, influenced by evolving clinical practices and an increase in maternal requests.
